core_obligations: Transfer parts (2) and (3) from deformation theory using the two identifications of the cotangent complex (proof lines 3184-3190).
For part (1), produce the class xi' in Ext^1_A(NL_{A/A'}, N) whose being in the image of the comparison map is equivalent to solvability (proof lines 3193-3215).
Rewrite xi' as a class on L_{A/A'} tensor_A^L B and identify the comparison map with the one appearing in the long exact sequence of the distinguished triangle (proof lines 3216-3223).
Take xi to be the image of xi' in Ext^2_B(L_{B/A}, N) and conclude both necessity and sufficiency (proof lines 3223-3224).
difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma with its three assertions: there is a canonical class xi in Ext^2_B(L_{B/A}, N) whose vanishing is necessary and sufficient for the existence of a solution to the lifting equation; when solutions exist their isomorphism classes form a principal homogeneous space under Ext^1_B(L_{B/A}, N); and the automorphisms of a given solution are canonically Ext^0_B(L_{B/A}, N) (source lines 3168-3182). Parts (2) and (3) are obtained by transferring the deformation-theory statements along the identifications of the naive cotangent complex with the truncation of the cotangent complex and of H^0 with the differentials. Part (1) is proved by exhibiting the deformation-theoretic class xi' in Ext^1_A(NL_{A/A'}, N), rewriting it as a class on L_{A/A'} tensor B, and observing that the long exact sequence of the triangle for A' -> A -> B shows that solvability is exactly the condition that xi' lie in the image of the comparison map, so that the image xi in Ext^2_B(L_{B/A}, N) is the obstruction.
